title: What is Loop Engineering?

What is Loop Engineering?
Loop engineering is all about replacing yourself as the person who prompts the agent.

Loop engineering means designing how the system chooses that next step.
You still own the outcome.

title: Goal: make the test suite 20% faster
text:
Goal: make the test suite 20% faster

Start once with /goal. Replace the highlighted fields for your project.
LOOP ENGINEERING
12
Goal
/goal Make the full test suite at least [20%] faster.
Trigger
Start when I submit this goal.
Action
Record the median of [3] full runs on the same runner.
Profile the slowest work. Change one shared cause.
Check + save
Rerun the same suite [3] times after each change.
Keep changes only when tests pass and timing improves.
Preserve every test, assertion, fixture, and coverage target.
Save timings, the diff, and the next idea in [loop-state.md].
Repeat + stop
Repeat until the [20%] improvement is verified.
Stop after [3 changes] or [25 minutes], or if blocked.
Leave a local diff for review. Do not merge or deploy.
notes:
This is a copyable workshop prompt adapted from the named use case.
Read the goal, trigger, action, check, saved state, repetition rule, and stops in the prompt.
The percentages, time limits, and number of attempts are workshop choices, not measured results.
Goal mode continues work toward a condition. A scheduled loop starts another pass later.
Prompt limits are instructions. Use runner or platform controls for enforced time and spending ceilings.
For the scheduled example, keep the session open and confirm that the recurring task was cancelled after the third pass.
For the alert example, the alert supplies evidence; an engineer submits the goal. Automatic event delivery needs a CI integration or channel.
Do not present a slash command as a production event listener.
The complete prompt is included below.

/goal Make the full test suite at least 20% faster.
Trigger: start when I submit this goal.
Record the median of 3 full runs on the same runner.
Profile the slowest work. Change one shared cause.
Rerun the same suite 3 times after each change.
Keep changes only when tests pass and timing improves.
Preserve every test, assertion, fixture, and coverage target.
Save timings, the diff, and the next idea in loop-state.md.
Repeat until the 20% improvement is verified.
Stop after 3 changes or 25 minutes, or if blocked.
Leave a local diff for review. Do not merge or deploy.

Write the prompt for your own loop

Replace every highlighted field with a detail from your own task.

39
Goal
/goal Reach [a result you can check].
Trigger
Start when [the trigger happens].
Action
Inspect [the current evidence].
Change one [allowed unit of work].
Check + save
Run [the same check] after each change.
Save [the result and next idea].
Repeat + stop
Repeat until [the goal is verified].
Stop at [success, a limit, or a need for a person].
notes:
Give learners five minutes to write one prompt.

For the RAG exercise, require the expected approved source first in all three retrieval checks.
Keep answer-quality review separate.

/goal Make the full suite [20%] faster.

title: Run one bounded loop. Keep the evidence.
text:
Run one bounded loop. Keep the evidence.

LOOP ENGINEERING
41
BEFORE YOU START

What could fake a pass?

What if one check fails twice?

What must stay fixed?

How will you spot a bad checker?

What will a reviewer see?

RUN LIMITS

✓
isolated branch or worktree

✓
one unit of work

✓
memory stays current

✓
every check runs

✓
stop at success, 3 failures, or 25 min

✓
no merge, deploy, publish, or messages
notes:
This is the hands-on lab.
Use a prepared worktree.
Run one attempt against the frozen check.
Keep the first failure visible.
Save the score, hypothesis, diff, and next step.

Stop at success, three repeated failures, or 25 minutes.
Do not merge, deploy, publish, or send messages.

At the end, each learner gives one verdict:
Approve, reject, or ask for another check.
They must point to evidence for that decision.

Debrief:
Did this save engineering work?
Ask what was accepted, what evidence justified it, and how much review it needed.
Do not equate more attempts or a green lab score with value.
For the RAG exercise, the automatic goal covers retrieval.
Review saved answers separately.
A broader answer-quality loop needs human labels and a calibrated judge.
